A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMGM study. All 19 pages of each version, including Appendices A–E, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original OMGM retrieval and VQA results, ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative examples, including the OK-VQA evaluation in Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results. The OK-VQA and efficiency studies now appear in the main text, while additional ablations and case studies remain in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same summary-based entity search, Q-Former multimodal reranking, cross-step similarity fusion and section selection. The training objective, inference procedures and prompt templates are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate E-VQA, InfoSeek and OK-VQA. The OK-VQA study moves from v1 Appendix D.1 to v2 Section 4.4, retaining the same document-structure generalization scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the matched experiments. Tables 2–3 retain their baseline sets, and Tables 8–9 retain PreFLMR and, for the efficiency comparison, LLaVA-1.5-7B.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendices B–C retain the same sample counts, splits, metrics, training settings and retrieval parameters, including k = 20, alpha = 0.9 and beta = 0.2. The relocated efficiency study retains its query-embedding and similarity-matching timing protocol.

E4.justification: The retrieval-step, modality, retrieval-scope, similarity-computation and fusion-weight ablations are retained, alongside generator comparisons and Appendix E case studies. The generalization and efficiency analyses are relocated without changing their evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plots and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 8 reports OMGM Pseudo Recall@5 of 73.4 and VQA score of 66.57 in both versions; Table 9 retains its 0.402-second average retrieval time.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical definitions, contrastive loss and similarity-fusion rules. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about granularity-aligned multistep retrieval, state-of-the-art retrieval performance and competitive VQA results. The reformatted contribution list preserves its scientific meaning.

C2.justification: The explanations of granularity alignment, similarity fusion, generalization and efficiency are retained. The Limitations section and Appendix E preserve the qualifications concerning unused secondary images and generators’ difficulties interpreting retrieved knowledge.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. The prompts, checkpoints, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time details in Appendices A–C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. The positioning against PreFLMR in the generalization and efficiency studies is retained when those studies move into the main text.

P1.justification: v2 converts the contribution paragraph into bullets and incorporates v1 Appendices D.1–D.2 into Section 4.4. The remaining Appendix D subsections and cross-references are updated, with only small wording edits elsewhere.

P2.justification: Tables 8–9 move from the appendix into the main text, and several existing tables and plots are repositioned as the text reflows. Figure artwork, table structures and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a concrete code-access pointer and makes the existing generalization and efficiency evidence easier to find in the main experimental narrative. The clearer contribution list also aids readability. These are limited improvements in access and presentation; the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
